rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the highest-priority uncertainty is establishing a clean, interpretable performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the space: it uses a fast linear encoder (PCA), avoids image processing and aggregation complexity, and isolates the RNA signal alone. This gives a low-variance reference point against which every subsequent design choice (better encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, fusion strategy) can be measured. It is also the cheapest experiment to run, preserving budget for more informative follow-ups. Once I have this RNA-only baseline, the next logical step is an image-only baseline (config_010) and then a simple multimodal config (config_016) to directly test whether and how much the image modality adds value.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485), the dominant uncertainty is whether the image modality carries useful signal at all. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides the cleanest possible single-variable comparison: it changes only the modality while holding profile_setting=singleprofile constant and using a standard, well-understood encoder (resnet50) to avoid confounding training instability. If image accuracy substantially exceeds or falls below the RNA baseline, we immediately know whether to prioritize multimodal fusion or invest in improving the RNA encoder/aggregation. If they are similar, we learn that neither modality alone is sufficient and multimodal fusion becomes the key lever. This is the highest-information experiment under a limited budget because it resolves the most consequential design question (which modality to build on) before spending further experiments on encoder or aggregation variants within a single modality.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% acc while image (resnet50, singleprofile) achieves only 20.8% acc, a gap of ~28 points. This raises a critical uncertainty: is the image modality fundamentally uninformative for this task, or is resnet50 simply an inadequate encoder? Question tested: config_013 (image_only, singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l) isolates the image encoder variable by swapping resnet50 for a much stronger pretrained ViT-L while keeping all other settings identical. Why this is the best next experiment: the result will determine the entire search direction. If ViT-L substantially improves image accuracy, multimodal fusion (configs 022-051) becomes a high-priority exploitation path. If it does not, the image modality is likely a dead end and budget should be redirected to RNA-only improvements (multiprofile, better encoders). With only 2 experiments completed, resolving this fork-in-the-road uncertainty is more valuable than incrementally improving the already-stronger RNA modality, as it effectively halves the remaining search space and prevents wasting budget on multimodal configs built on a weak image signal.

Evidence: RNA-only with pca_n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% acc, while both image-only models perform poorly (~21-23%), suggesting image features alone are weak. However, it remains unclear whether image features provide complementary information in a multimodal context. Question tested: Does concatenating image features (resnet50) to the RNA representation improve over RNA-only? config_016 is the minimal multimodal extension of config_001 (same RNA encoder, same singleprofile setting, only adding resnet50 image via concat), giving a clean A/B comparison. Why this is the best next experiment: With only 3 data points, the most fundamental design decision is whether the multimodal paradigm adds value at all. Resolving this early prevents wasting budget on 36 multimodal configurations if image features are uninformative, or confirms a promising direction to exploit. The simple concat fusion also avoids confounding from more complex fusion strategies.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, PCA n2000 + ResNet50, concat) is the best result so far (acc 0.527, F1 0.510), showing a modest ~4pp gain over RNA-alone (0.485). All completed experiments use singleprofile; the multiprofile + aggregation axis is completely untested and represents a major design uncertainty. Question: Does aggregating multiple profiles (via avgpool) in the multimodal setting improve over the single-profile baseline, and if so, by how much? Why this config: config_018 is the minimal, direct extension of the current best (config_016) along the single untested dimension (profile/aggregation), keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion strategy identical. This isolates the multiprofile+avgpool effect, reducing uncertainty about whether profile aggregation is worth the added complexity before investing further experiments in transformer aggregation or alternative fusion. Under a tight budget, this one experiment tells us whether the multiprofile axis is worth exploring at all, making it the highest-information next step.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile multimodal (config_018, acc=0.619) dramatically outperforms singleprofile multimodal (config_016, acc=0.527), a +9.2% jump driven by the multiprofile setting with avgpool aggregation. The only untested dimension within this best-performing family is the aggregation method: we have only seen avgpool. Config_020 changes exactly one variable (aggregation: avgpool → transformer) while holding all else constant (pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion, multiprofile). This directly tests whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer, which can model inter-profile relationships) can further improve over the simple average pool, or whether the gain from multiprofile is already captured by averaging. Under a limited budget, this clean single-variable ablation on the most impactful design axis (how multiple profiles are combined) maximizes information gain: a positive result opens a high-performing direction, while a null/negative result confirms avgpool suffices and redirects effort toward other levers (fusion strategy, image encoder).

The current best (config_018, acc=0.619) uses concat fusion in a multimodal multiprofile setup with avgpool aggregation. We have only tested concat fusion across all multimodal experiments, so the fusion strategy remains a major untested design axis. Config_019 is a controlled A/B test against config_018, changing only fusion from concat to weighted while holding all other factors (pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, multiprofile) constant. This directly answers whether the two modalities benefit from learned weighting versus simple concatenation. Given that RNA dominates (0.485 vs ~0.21 for image), a weighted scheme could down-weight the weaker image signal and sharpen the RNA contribution, potentially yielding a meaningful gain. If it does not improve, we cleanly rule out fusion as a lever and redirect budget toward encoder upgrades (scvi/scgpt or ViT-L). Under a limited budget, this single-variable comparison to the current best is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step.

Evidence: The current best config (config_019: pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.639 acc. All multimodal results so far use pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder; the RNA encoder axis is completely untested. RNA dominates image performance (0.485 vs ~0.21–0.23 image-only), so the quality of the RNA representation likely has the largest leverage on final multimodal accuracy. Question: Does a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) provide a meaningfully better representation than linear PCA, when fused with the known-best image/aggregation/fusion settings? Why this is the best next experiment: It isolates the single largest untested design axis (RNA encoder) while holding all other parameters at their empirically validated best values (multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool, weighted). A positive result would justify further exploration of scgpt; a null result would confirm PCA sufficiency and redirect budget toward the image-encoder axis (e.g., config_025). This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: The current best (config_031, 0.678 acc) uses scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + avgpool + weighted. All other axes (profile, aggregation, fusion, RNA encoder) have been validated as beneficial. The one major untested dimension in this best configuration is the image encoder: ViT-L outperformed ResNet50 in image-only (0.227 vs 0.208), but we have no evidence for how a stronger image encoder interacts with the multimodal pipeline. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l (while keeping all other settings at their known-best values) further improve validation accuracy, or is the image contribution already saturated with ResNet50? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean, single-variable extension of the current best, resolving high-impact uncertainty about whether the image modality can be leveraged more effectively. If it helps, it identifies a clear path to further gains; if it does not, it tells us to focus remaining budget on RNA-side improvements (e.g., scgpt) rather than image-side upgrades.

The current best (config_037: scVI, ViT-L, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.706 acc. The evidence strongly supports multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion, and ViT-L as the optimal settings for all parameters except the RNA encoder. The RNA encoder axis shows clear progression (PCA 0.639 → scVI 0.678), but scGPT is completely untested in the multimodal setting. Config_049 (scGPT, ViT-L, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) isolates the scGPT variable while holding all other parameters at their best-known values, directly testing whether a more advanced generative RNA encoder can outperform scVI. This is the highest-uncertainty, highest-value experiment: if scGPT exceeds scVI it yields a new best configuration; if it underperforms, it confirms scVI as the optimal encoder and redirects budget toward other refinements (e.g., transformer aggregation re-test or fusion variants). No other untested configuration addresses such a large unexplored dimension under otherwise optimal settings.
